\section{Project Summary}
\label{\detokenize{project_summary:project-summary}}\label{\detokenize{project_summary::doc}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{project_summary:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The StarSync Network project was executed on April 07, 2026 with the goal of
establishing automated repository synchronization across multiple development
endpoints. The project deployed a cron\sphinxhyphen{}based sync infrastructure on two
reachable machines (laptop and Command AWS), with GitHub as the central hub.

\section{Lessons Learned}
\label{\detokenize{lessons_learned:lessons-learned}}\label{\detokenize{lessons_learned::doc}}

\subsection{Technical}
\label{\detokenize{lessons_learned:technical}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Disk space awareness} \textendash{} Old Sphinx builds were consuming significant
disk space on /home. Clearing them freed 375MB. Recommendation: run
build cleanup as part of the sync process or add a cron job for periodic
build artifact cleanup.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Herd immunity for sync} \textendash{} Skipping repos with \textgreater{}500 changes proved
effective. The sync continued working for all other repos rather than
failing entirely due to one problematic repository.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SSH key management} \textendash{} Using paperclip\sphinxhyphen{}hermes\sphinxhyphen{}nvidia\sphinxhyphen{}key.pem for AWS
authentication worked reliably. No authentication failures during
deployment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Package naming} \textendash{} The pip package for Honcho memory is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{honcho\sphinxhyphen{}ai}}
not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{honcho}}. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{honcho}} package on PyPI is a Process Manager
(Foreman clone). This ambiguity caused an initial installation error.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Process}
\label{\detokenize{lessons_learned:process}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Documentation order} \textendash{} Writing documents in Mandate \(\rightarrow\) Brief \(\rightarrow\) Plan \(\rightarrow\)
Highlight order proved effective. Each document builds on the previous
one and follows a logical flow from requirements to outcomes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Telegram as notification layer} \textendash{} Telegram delivered PR URLs reliably
and quickly. HTML formatting makes messages clear with clickable links.
This is a proven channel for agent\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}human communication.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Agent fallback value} \textendash{} While not yet triggered, the architecture is
sound. The ability for cron failures to automatically spawn an agent
in YOLO mode means zero\sphinxhyphen{}touch recovery for most sync issues.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Recommendations}
\label{\detokenize{lessons_learned:recommendations}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Add build step to sync} \textendash{} Include Sphinx build as part of the sync
script so doc changes are compiled automatically.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Monitor disk usage} \textendash{} Add disk space check to the sync script and
alert if /home exceeds 90\% usage.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reach aws\sphinxhyphen{}ai} \textendash{} Resolve SSH connectivity to the AI AWS endpoint
to complete the three\sphinxhyphen{}node star network.

\end{enumerate}
